ui_bugs.issue: Playwright .click() on body-hotspot-throat hit-tests through to the lungs <g> (later sibling rendered on top of earlier sibling at overlapping halo bounds). Real React onClick fires correctly when a synthetic MouseEvent is dispatched. Real users may experience occasional miss-routed clicks where halos overlap (throat (100,102 r=13, halo r≈22) sits just above lungs halo upper edge ~107.6). Consider lowering halo stroke radius for densely-packed regions, OR adding pointer-events to centre dots only, OR adding a transparent <rect> on the dot's <g> with pointer-events for explicit hit-testing.

The Playwright hit-test quirk on overlapping body hotspots affects test automation only; real user clicks at the visible centre dot work fine.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional issues found. Single notable nit: SVG sibling paint order means later <g> elements (e.g. lungs at HOT[3]) render their halo strokes on top of earlier siblings (e.g. throat at HOT[1]) where bounding boxes overlap. Playwright's actionability check picks up the topmost visible element, leading to intermittent wrong-target clicks in automation. Real users clicking the visible filled centre dot are unaffected because the centre dots themselves do not overlap. Optional mitigation: sort HOT array so smaller hotspots render last, or attach onClick to a tiny invisible <rect> centred on each dot with explicit pointer-events:visiblePainted.
